writeup: TIC 308578336 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 17.45 percent and completes its orbital cycle every 4.2766 days. A secondary eclipse was detected at a phase of 0.30 with 7.3 sigma significance, suggesting a close binary pair. The automated detection achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 179.8 using the Box Least Squares method, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 73.7. The source does not appear in six cross-checked variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown candidate. While the machine-learning screening score of 0.36 indicates moderate confidence, the candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
